summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of Factor V Leiden deficiency, asplenia, chronic cough, COPD, and incisional hernia was admitted for worsening cough, sinus congestion, and a prior low-grade fever. Chest X-ray showed no pneumonia, and strep test was negative, supporting a diagnosis of viral upper respiratory infection. He was treated with cefpodoxime given his asplenic status, along with bronchodilators and cough suppressants. His chronic conditions, including anticoagulation with Lovenox, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and hernia, were monitored and remained stable. Simvastatin was dose-reduced from 80 mg to 40 mg daily per safety guidelines. He improved clinically, remained afebrile, and was discharged home with a short course of antibiotics and symptomatic treatments, with follow-up advised with his primary care provider.
